title: Initiative: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools (beta → GA)
creator: Marissa Cole
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Context
Dedicated customers run on reserved GPU pools with strict isolation + SLAs. Today our rollout story for Dedicated is effectively pool-level “all at once” (or manual, error-prone sequencing), which creates unacceptable blast radius: bad model/runtime/config changes can saturate a reserved pool, increase queue depth, and violate p95 latency / availability commitments.

This initiative implements first-class staged rollouts for Dedicated pools:
- Multi-stage rollout plans (Stage 0 internal/shadow → Stage 1 5% → Stage 2 25% → Stage 3 100% is the baseline example)
- Gate evaluation per stage (latency, 5xx/timeouts, GPU utilization, queue depth; quality signals optional where available)
- Manual approvals and automated holds/rollbacks when thresholds fail
- Auditable state changes (who approved, what changed, when) and safe behavior under partial failures
- Routing/policy integration so allocations are deterministic and respect tenant isolation

Primary target users (v1)
- Redwood operators (SRE + platform operations)
- Enterprise opt-in Dedicated tenants with explicit enablement + scoped permissions

Non-goals (v1)
- Full self-serve for all Dedicated tenants
- Multi-armed bandit experimentation (A/B remains separate; may share primitives later)
- Per-request semantic quality gating for all routes (only optional/select workloads)

Milestones (planned)
1) Discovery + requirements alignment (Product/Dedicated/SRE/Security)
- Outcome: PRD v1 complete; default gates + escalation policy drafted; beta scope locked.

2) Platform primitives (control plane + APIs)
- RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate data model, persistence + migrations
- CRUD + status APIs; idempotency and optimistic concurrency
- Approval/abort endpoints and audit event emission

3) Policy + routing integration (Dedicated pools)
- Deterministic traffic allocation per stage weights
- Guardrails: 0%/100% transitions, safe fallback behavior, tenant isolation invariants

4) Gate evaluator + telemetry hardening
- Reliable evaluation windows; cardinality controls
- Fail-safe behavior on missing/late metrics (pause/hold rather than proceed)
- Evaluator health SLOs + dashboards/alerts

5) Console workflows
- Create/edit rollout wizard
- Stage detail view: gate status + evaluation windows + recent failures
- Approve/abort flow with RBAC checks and audit surfacing

6) Operational readiness
- Runbooks (paused rollouts, rollback, incident response)
- Load tests on reserved pools; perf canaries
- Feature flags + allowlist enablement; release train plan

7) Beta → GA
- Dogfood on Redwood-managed Dedicated pools
- Beta with 2–3 enterprise customers
- GA with documented defaults + backwards compatibility

Beta entry criteria (must-have)
- Feature flag: Dedicated-only enablement; per-tenant allowlist + operator override
- Stage progression works end-to-end (create → stage allocation → gate eval → approve → advance)
- Gate failure behavior: auto-hold within the evaluation window; no automatic advance if evaluator degraded
- Audit events emitted for: create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold/auto-rollback (as applicable)
- Dashboards: per-pool rollout status, evaluator lag, gate evaluation success rate
- Runbook for paused rollout validated by oncall (tabletop)

Beta success criteria (quantitative + qualitative)
- At least 2 beta tenants complete ≥2 rollouts each with staged gating enabled
- Zero incidents caused by rollout system violating tenant isolation or routing determinism
- 95%+ of gate evaluations succeed without “metrics missing” holds in steady state (after initial tuning)
- Operator feedback: approval + investigation flow usable without bespoke scripts

GA launch criteria
- SRE sign-off on: evaluator health alerts, stuck/paused rollouts alerts, escalation routing
- Security sign-off on: RBAC matrix for enterprise scopes; audit log retention/export compatibility
- Documented defaults: recommended gates + thresholds for Dedicated (with tuning guidance)
- Backwards compatibility: existing pool-level changes continue to work (no forced migration); staged rollout is additive
- Known limitations clearly communicated in GA notes (e.g., quality signals availability)

Risks / open questions
- Metrics freshness: avoid “metrics lie” / delayed ingestion leading to bad decisions; need explicit freshness checks and UI surfacing.
- Autoscaling/headroom: partial stage allocations can overconcentrate load and inflate queue depth; guardrails required (minimum headroom rules).
- Customer permissions: right balance of operator control vs enterprise self-serve; keep v1 narrow.
- Rollback semantics: clarify what “rollback” means for Dedicated pools (previous plan version vs previous model version vs routing weight reset).

comments: 2025-01-07 (Marissa Cole): Creating initiative epic to centralize beta/GA readiness. Dedicated rollouts have been a recurring source of support escalations (latency spikes during updates; lack of audit trail). Talia to drive program cadence and weekly stakeholder sync.

2025-01-10 (Talia Benson): Drafted milestone plan + asked SRE (Sean/Allison) to propose default gate thresholds and alerting. Security (Marcus) requested we treat audit events as SOC2-relevant change management artifacts; retention/export needs to be explicit in ADR-028.

2025-01-14 (Paula Mendes): PRD scope locked for beta: required gates = p95 latency, 5xx rate, timeout rate, queue depth, GPU utilization. Quality signals optional and explicitly out-of-scope for “required for beta.” Added requirement: missing/late metrics must pause (hold) rather than proceed.

2025-01-18 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated constraint callout: staged rollouts must not cause cross-tenant interference; routing must be deterministic per-request to avoid “flapping” between versions. Also need clear playbook for capacity constrained pools (what happens if headroom drops mid-stage).

2025-01-24 (Ethan Park): Control plane proposal reviewed. Strong preference for versioned RolloutPlan with optimistic concurrency + append-only approval/audit events. Need to ensure idempotency keys across create/update/approve endpoints (incidents have shown duplicate actions during retries).

2025-01-29 (Allison Grant): Observability requirements: evaluator lag SLO + alerts, plus “false positive hold rate” metric so we can tune thresholds. Also requested a single dashboard panel per pool: current stage, weights, last gate eval, and last approval actor.

2025-02-03 (Marcus Lin): Security review notes: enterprise tenant scopes must be explicit (rollout.edit vs rollout.approve vs rollout.abort). Audit events must include actor type (user/service), tenant_id, pool_id, plan_version, and stage_id. Confirmed v1 can be operator-only for most customers, but must be ready for enterprise opt-in.

2025-02-10 (Talia Benson): Beta candidate selection in progress with CS (Rachel/Miguel). Criteria: history of painful model updates, willingness to participate in weekly check-ins, and ability to provide latency SLO targets. Target: 2–3 customers, staggered onboarding to reduce oncall load.

2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Oncall readiness gate: no beta enablement until pause/hold behavior is proven under missing metrics + evaluator degradation. Requested we run a tabletop using the paused-rollout runbook with a simulated queue-depth incident.

2025-02-21 (Marissa Cole): Adjusted due date to align with release train. GA criteria updated to include explicit backwards-compat story (staged rollouts additive) and customer-facing docs. Next: finalize beta entry checklist and confirm which customers get feature-flag allowlist first.
